land.text: Silla after the conquest of Baekje and of Goguryeo south of the Taedong River

predecessors.note: The same kingdom: the Silla page calls the period 'Unified Silla' and the infobox gives 'Later Silla: 668-935'. Cliopatria starts a new row in 682; the pages date the unification to 668 (Unified Silla infobox) or the end of the war with Tang in 676.

land.text: Silla's rump, the Gyeongsang region round Gyeongju

successors.note: Gyeongsun 'submitted to Wang Geon' in 935 (no month on the page). Hubaekje and Taebong took the south-west and the north earlier.

capitals.name: Seorabeol (Gyeongju)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Seorabeol (present-day Gyeongju)'; Gyeongju 'remained the capital of Silla throughout the whole existence of the dynasty'.

correction.text: Silla south of the Taedong River without Jeju, which is Tamna under a tributary tint

keyframe_review.note: 149,880 km2 for 682-891. After the Silla-Tang War Silla 'controlled most of the Korean Peninsula' with a line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay' (the outline reaches 40.1 N, a little beyond that line). The Unified Silla infobox gives no area (population 6,000,000 in the 8th century). Cliopatria folds Jeju into this shape; the Tamna page has Tamna a tributary of Silla (662-925), and the Tamna dossier keeps the island as Tamna's from 682, so Jeju is removed.

correction.text: Silla without Later Baekje's south-west and without Jeju; valid 892-900

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts 24,800 km2 for Later Baekje in 892 ('In 892, Kyŏn Hwŏn seized the cities of Wansanju and Mujinju'). The centre and north stay in the shape to 910 although Kung Ye held them from 901 (Kaesong) and 905 (Pyongyang, 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla', Gungye page); the shape is valid 892-900 only, 901-904 is unified-silla_901 and from 905 unified-silla_905. Jeju removed. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 892..900 from this entry's own 'valid 892-900 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Silla without Later Baekje's south-west, without Jeju and without the Kaesong region Kung Ye holds from 901

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (fix round): Kung Ye 'proclaim[ed] himself king of Later Goguryeo' in 901 after his rebellion 'in present-day Kaesong in 898' (Gungye page), so the 100 km circle round Kaesong (35,659 km2 inside the 892 outline, taebong_901's core) is Taebong's from 901, not Silla's. The rest of the centre and north stays in Silla to 904, as before.

correction.text: Silla reduced to its south-east, from 905

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kung Ye's Later Goguryeo holds the centre and north from 905, so Silla is the Gyeongsang rump (Cliopatria's 911 outline, 38,421 km2) six years before Cliopatria draws it. Fix round: this shape also drops about 11,100 km2 of Cliopatria's 892 outline between 39.4 and 40.1 N (south Hamgyong-namdo, north-east South Pyongan) that is in neither Cliopatria's Unified Silla 911 nor its Taebong 911; see the 905 loss to nobody in the ledger.
38,421 km2 for 911-925, the Gyeongsang region (about 40,000 km2 of Silla's heartland) with Jeju and a little of Gangwon and the south-west. Jeju removed. The pages date no other loss until 928.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 926 shape without Jeju and, from 928, without Jinju

keyframe_review.note: Same 38,421 km2. 'In 927, Kyŏn Hwŏn led his army himself and directly attacked the Silla capital of Gyeongju.' 'One year later he took over the city of Jinju from Silla.' (Gyeon Hwon page), so Jinju leaves the shape from 928; Gyeongsun submits to Goryeo in 935 (Unified Silla page, no month). Jeju removed.

region.text: Silla after the unification of the peninsula south of the Taedong

ledger.note: 682: Silla appears as 'Unified Silla' on the map. Same kingdom as the Silla dossier: Cliopatria opens a new row in 682 (King Sinmun, 681-692), the infobox dates 'Unified Korea: 668' and the Silla-Tang War ended in 676. Start year is a bridge to the Cliopatria row. Fix round: the Sinmun of Silla page gives 'Coronation: 681' and says he 'came to power in the immediate wake of Silla's unification of the peninsula', with no Taedong line and no 682; the start year stays a bridge to Cliopatria's row.

region.text: Jeju Island, the kingdom of Tamna

ledger.note: 682: Tamna, a tributary of Silla since 662, stays so ('Tributary state of Silla (662-925)', Tamna infobox); the relation began in the Silla dossier and is restated here because the dossier changes in 682. The page says Tamna 'officially subjugated itself to Silla' without a year in the text.

892: Kyŏn Hwŏn seizes the south-west. 'In 892, Kyŏn Hwŏn seized the cities of Wansanju and Mujinju'; the Later Three Kingdoms page lists 889 (the first rebellions), 892 and 900 as candidate starts of the period. The region is Cliopatria's Hubaekje outline.

region.text: Songak/Kaesong, where Kung Ye rebelled in 898 and proclaimed Later Goguryeo in 901

ledger.note: 901: Kung Ye proclaims Later Goguryeo at Kaesong. 'Kung Ye instigated his own rebellion in present-day Kaesŏng in 898' and went on 'to proclaim himself king of Later Goguryeo' in 901 (Gungye page; Taebong page: 'a state established by Kung Ye on the Korean Peninsula in 901'). Mirror of taebong /ledger/0: the 100 km circle round Kaesong (35,659 km2) lies wholly inside Cliopatria's Unified Silla 892 outline, so it leaves Silla in 901. The page does not say Silla lost the land in a war; the circle is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the centre and north taken by Kung Ye, outside the Kaesong core lost in 901: Cliopatria's Taebong 911 outline without the Kaesong circle, plus the Pyongyang circle's part of Silla's 892 outline

ledger.note: c.905: Silla loses the centre and north to Kung Ye. 'In the same year Kung Ye took over Pyongyang and called for total destruction of the state of Silla', 'taking control of almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla' (Gungye page); the year is the page's implicit 905, the year after 'Kung Ye changed the country's name to Majin in 904', and the Cheorwon move is 'in the following year'. The page dates only Pyongyang; the rest is a bridge. The region is the mirror of taebong /ledger/3 and /ledger/4 (Pyongyang circle, then Taebong's 911 outline outside the Kaesong and Pyongyang circles); fix round: it no longer subtracts the Pyongyang circle, 24,800 km2 of which lies inside Silla's 892 outline, and it excludes the Kaesong circle already lost in 901. Cliopatria draws the loss in 911.

region.text: the strip between 39.4 and 40.1 N that Cliopatria's 892 outline holds beyond the Taedong-to-East-Korea-Bay line, outside the Pyongyang circle

ledger.note: c.905: the northern edge of Cliopatria's outline passes to nobody. 9,400 km2 (grid) in south Hamgyong-namdo and north-east South Pyongan lie in Cliopatria's Unified Silla 892 outline but in neither its 911 outline nor Taebong's. The Silla-Tang War page gives the limit as the line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay', which this strip lies beyond (unified-silla_682 note: 'a little beyond'); no page names the land or dates its loss. 905 is chosen because it is the year Kung Ye's state and the shrunken Silla outline of unified-silla_905 appear. The alternative, cutting the strip from unified-silla_682 and _892 and silla_676, is not done because the page's line is not precise enough to place the cut.
925: the end of Tamna's tributary status to Silla ('Tributary state of Silla (662-925)', Tamna infobox); Goryeo's lordship over the island starts in 938.

c.928: Later Baekje takes Jinju. 'In 927, Kyŏn Hwŏn led his army himself and directly attacked the Silla capital of Gyeongju.' 'One year later he took over the city of Jinju from Silla.' (Gyeon Hwon page; the year 928 is inferred from the two sentences). In 927 Kyŏn Hwŏn had sacked the capital, killed King Gyeongae and installed Gyeongsun (Later Baekje page).

region.text: Silla's remaining Gyeongsang region, passing whole to Goryeo

ledger.note: 935: Gyeongsun submits to Goryeo. 'Gyeongsun submitted to Wang Geon' of Goryeo, ending the dynasty (infobox 'Handover to the Goryeo: 935'; Goryeo page: 'the peaceful annexation of Later Silla in 935'). No month on either page.

wars.name: Tang-Balhae War
wars.outcome: Balhae raided Dengzhou in 732; Xuanzong ordered a Tang-Silla attack in 733 that was repelled (snow); Silla attacked Balhae without success in 734; Balhae made peace with Tang in 737.
wars.note: The Mu of Balhae page dates the Silla attack to 733, the Balhae page to 734 (used). The Tang stationed troops in the Paegang region at Silla's request in 735 (Balhae page).

wars.name: Later Three Kingdoms
wars.outcome: Silla lost the south-west to Later Baekje (892) and the centre and north to Kung Ye (c.905); Gyeongsun submitted to Goryeo in 935 and Later Baekje fell in 936.
wars.note: The Later Three Kingdoms page calls the start dates 'loosely defined' (889, 892, 900) and the end 935 or 936; the Unified Silla infobox gives 892-936.

wars.name: Later Baekje's sack of Gyeongju
wars.outcome: Kyŏn Hwŏn killed King Gyeongae and put Gyeongsun on the throne; Taejo was beaten near Daegu.

certainty.note: The northern line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay' was recognised by Tang in 736 (Silla-Tang War page), but no survey or treaty fixes it; the frontier with Balhae is approximate.
The fronts with Later Baekje and Kung Ye move year by year without a stated line.

notes: Silla and Unified Silla are one kingdom with two Cliopatria rows (378-681, 682-935): the Silla page uses both labels, and 668/676 (pages) and 682 (Cliopatria) are three candidate dates for the change. Two dossiers are kept because the orchestrator listed two slugs; the colour agent should give them one colour (rule 2). Cliopatria folds Jeju into this row 682-935; removed here in every keyframe because the Tamna dossier keeps the island as a tributary state (Tamna infobox: Silla tributary 662-925). The Unified Silla page is thin (no Taedong line, no Hasoju wall, no nine provinces, no Gungye/Gyeon Hwon dates); the Silla page, the Silla-Tang War page and the two Later Three Kingdoms biographies filled the gaps. 735/736: 'A formal Tang recognition of Sillan sovereignty over the Korean Peninsula south of the Taedong River occurred in 736' (Silla-Tang War page) changes no border, so it is in the war outcome, not a ledger event. No area on the Unified Silla page, so no infobox comparison was possible. Pages cited: Unified Silla, Silla-Tang War, Gungye, Gyeon Hwon, Balhae, Tamna (six against a budget of 5; the Silla, Later Three Kingdoms and Mu of Balhae pages were also read). The Cliopatria Silla/Taebong boundary of 911 is moved to 905 (see unified-silla_905); the gazetteer lacks Jinju. Fix round (2026-10-19): (1) a 901 loss of the Kaesong circle to taebong (mirror of taebong /ledger/0), new keyframe unified-silla_901, unified-silla_892 valid 892-900. (2) The 905 loss now mirrors taebong /ledger/3 and /ledger/4: Taebong 911 outline without the Kaesong circle, plus the Pyongyang circle's part of the 892 outline. (3) About 9,400 km2 between 39.4 and 40.1 N that Cliopatria draws in Silla to 904 and neither Silla 911 nor Taebong holds afterwards go to nobody in 905 (confidence 1, no page); not cut from unified-silla_682/892 because the Silla-Tang War page's line is not precise (disagreement with the reviewer's first option, which would also have changed silla_676). (4) The Jinju quotes are the Gyeon Hwon page's own sentences. Not settled: the 905 centre-and-north loss stays a bridge (the Later Three Kingdoms page is silent on Kung Ye; the Gungye page dates only Pyongyang, and only implicitly), and the 682 found event stays a bridge (the Sinmun page gives 681 and no Taedong line).
